source_data: data/missions.json (mission ids, objectives, rewards, unlocks — quoted verbatim)
data/professions.json (11 profession ids, workplaces, gameplay summaries)
data/npc-cast.json (25 cast ids npc_01..npc_25; trees are per situation, not per NPC)
notes: Authored data, not generated text (GDD-15 §11). Every line is written here; the Phase 6 runtime walks the trees and never authors a line.

Placeholders in angle brackets are filled at runtime from data that already exists, never invented: <name> = the speaking NPC's cast name, <life_goal> = the NPC's goal-stack life goal (GDD-01 §2.2), <current_work> = the NPC's current work sub-state (GDD-06 §4), <zone_name> = the display name of the NPC's current zone (GDD-02 §2).

No line references a fact the data does not hold: no invented NPC names, relatives, places, prices, or rewards. Zone lines use only the contents GDD-02 §2 lists for that zone; profession lines use only the workplace and gameplay summary professions.json carries for that profession.

Rewards are quoted verbatim from missions.json. Each mission tree carries rewards_quoted and objectives_quoted copied exactly from missions.json; the verifier checks them field-for-field. Mission 1.3 and 2.4 both have credits_ncr null — their lines say so plainly instead of inventing a credit amount.

Debt amounts are never stated in a line: a debt's amount lives in the ledger, and the ledger_settlement effect reads it from there (amount_ref ledger_debt_amount). Dialogue never creates or erases a debt (GDD-15 §4).

The apology weight reduction has no number in any source: GDD-15 §4 says only that the harming memory's weight is reduced, not deleted. The memory_weight_reduce effect therefore carries amount_ref runtime_rule and no invented number.

Memory weights are given only where a source gives one: +40 for the mission 1.3 completion memory (GDD-15 §5 worked example / §10 check 4). Other memory_write effects carry no weight; the runtime assigns it.

Speaker tokens: 'player' = the player; 'npc' = the speaking NPC, resolved at runtime to that NPC's cast id (trees are per situation, GDD-15 §5 rule 4); a profession id = an NPC of that profession template speaking a small-talk line.
Line counts: a node holds 1-3 lines (GDD-15 §5). Every line object and every node carries its own condition and effects fields per the §5 node contract.

condition_vocabulary.band: band:<close|warm|neutral|wary|hostile> — the §3 greeting band of the NPC's outgoing edge to the player
condition_vocabulary.band_min: band_min:<band> — band at least this warm
condition_vocabulary.band_max: band_max:<band> — band at most this warm
condition_vocabulary.relationship_mean_min: relationship_mean_min:<number> — mean of trust and affection toward the player at least this
condition_vocabulary.zone: zone:<zone id> — the NPC's current zone
condition_vocabulary.favour_available: favour_available:true|false — the side-mission generator has a favour for this NPC (GDD-04 §3)

effect_vocabulary.relationship_drift: type:relationship_drift, trust/affection/respect n — small drift per GDD-01 §4 step 4; big changes come only from events
effect_vocabulary.memory_write: type:memory_write, text:<...>, weight:<number, only when a source gives one>, tier:full — appends to character_memories (Full tier only)
effect_vocabulary.memory_weight_reduce: type:memory_weight_reduce, target:harming_episodic_memory, amount_ref:runtime_rule — weight reduced, never deleted (GDD-15 §4)
effect_vocabulary.mission_complete: type:mission_complete, mission_id:<id>, rewards:<verbatim missions.json rewards object>
effect_vocabulary.ledger_settlement: type:ledger_settlement, reason:repayment, amount_ref:ledger_debt_amount — settles an existing debt through the ledger's own functions only
effect_vocabulary.propose_goal: type:propose_goal, goal_ref:npc_life_goal — proposes a stage goal; the player accepts it or not, never silently applied
effect_vocabulary.none: type:none — explicitly no write (a decline, a refusal, a waiting answer)

greeting_bands.behaviour: Warm personal greeting, first-name, may open with an episodic memory (Full tier only).
Friendly greeting, topic menu opens with personal topics available.
Polite neutral greeting. The band for met_player = false (first meeting).
Short, guarded greeting; personal topics locked; mission offers refused until the band improves.
Refusal to talk, or a single hostile line and exit.

mission_1_3_neighbour_help.title: Know Your Neighbours
objectives_quoted: Help one neighbour with a small task (carry, fetch, fix)

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I'm <name>. I live two doors down — the blue door.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The market's that way — but my roof leaks and I can't climb. Could you carry these tiles up for me?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It's 'Know Your Neighbours': meet 3 neighbours, and help one neighbour with a small task — carry, fetch, fix. There are no credits in it. The reward is +10 reputation with each neighbour met and +5 district reputation, and it unlocks the Neighbour favour system.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Thank you. Come back when it's done — I'll have tea ready.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: No trouble — the tiles will wait.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Welcome to the district. The market's that way if you need anything.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The tiles are still waiting, whenever you have a moment. No rush — but the roof won't fix itself.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good. I'll put the kettle on for when you're done.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You did it! The tea's on — you're a good neighbour.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You're becoming a real friend, you know. I've been thinking — friends look out for each other in this city.

choices.text: What did you have in mind?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Raise one friendship to 40 or more — trust and affection both count. That's the whole of it: be a friend, properly.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: There's no credit reward. It gives +10 district reputation and a memory event, and it unlocks Friend favour missions.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good. Friends first, everything else second.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: No trouble — friendship isn't a job to apply for.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Another time, then. The offer stands — friends don't keep score.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: We're getting there. Keep showing up — that's what friendship is.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Look at us — proper friends now. The city feels smaller with you in it.

debt.title: Debt
debt.notes: Dialogue never creates or erases a debt — it only settles one the ledger already holds (GDD-15 §4). No line states an amount; the ledger_settlement effect reads the amount from the ledger.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I haven't forgotten — I owe you, and the ledger says so. I want to settle it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Here — settled in full, through the ledger, so there's a proper record of it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I can't pay it yet — I don't have it. Ask me again after payday, and I'll settle it.

effects.text: <name> could not repay a debt yet
<name> could not repay a debt yet

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Thank you for waiting. I'll settle it as soon as I can — the debt stands until then.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I don't like chasing money, but the ledger says you owe me. Can we settle it?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Here — paid in full, through the ledger.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Thank you. That's the end of it — no hard feelings.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: All right — but the debt stands, and I'll have to ask again.

effects.text: player asked for more time to repay a debt
player asked for more time to repay a debt

apology.title: Apology
apology.notes: One apology per offence (GDD-15 §4). On acceptance the harming memory's weight is reduced, not deleted; the reduction step is a runtime rule, not authored here.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm sorry about what happened. I was wrong.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Sorry doesn't undo it. Tell me why I should believe you.

choices.text: I mean it — let me make it right.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: All right. I remember it — I won't forget it — but I forgive you. Don't make me regret it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Then we're done talking. Come back when you actually mean it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You already apologised for that once. Once is all you get — the rest is up to how you act now.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I have nothing to say to you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: There you are! Sit — I was just thinking about you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good to see you! How's your day going?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Hello. Can I help you with something?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Yes? What do you want?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: What are you doing here?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm new here — I just moved in.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I'm <name>. Good to meet you — welcome to the district.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I'm not supposed to talk to strangers.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Work? Right now I'm <current_work> — that's where the day goes.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ask me again after my shift and I'll tell you how it really went.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Same as always — the work doesn't stop, but neither do I.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My goal right now is <life_goal>.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Maybe. Ask me again when the time's right — I'll know it when I see it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The family is doing well. We look after each other — that's how it works in this house.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You'll meet them when there's a reason to. Family isn't a tour.

ask_about_place.notes: One line per zone, from the contents GDD-02 §2 lists for that zone. <zone_name> is the zone's display name from GDD-02 §2.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: This is Boro Bazar — the market hall, the shop units, the tea stalls. If you need anything, it starts here.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Old Town Lanes — the oldest housing in the district. Narrow lanes, repair workshops, and neighbours who all know each other.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The riverfront and the ghat — the launch terminal, the fish market edge, and the promenade when the evening comes.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Midtown Residences — six-storey apartment blocks, including the building with the starter flats.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Civic Quarter — school, clinic, bank, police station, city office. Everything official lives here.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: College Para — the college building, the library, the student hostels, and the photocopy row.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Industry Edge — three small factories, the taxi and CNG depot, and the construction yard.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Central Park — the pond, the walking loop, the benches. The district breathes here.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Station Quarter — the bus terminal, the railway station, the rickshaw and CNG stands. Everyone passes through here eventually.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Uptown Heights — luxury apartments, the office block, and the rooftop restaurant. The district's high end.

mission_offer.unlock: NPC is the giver of an available mission

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I might have something for you — ask me about it and I'll tell you plainly, rewards and all.

choices.text: Tell me about 'A Friend in the City'.

favour.unlock: Side-mission generator has one for this NPC (GDD-04 §3)
favour.notes: The errand reward pattern is quoted verbatim from missions.json side_mission_types ('200-2,000 NCr + relationship') as a pattern, never as a promise for a specific favour.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A favour? Errands, lending a hand, mediating — that's the shape of it. The going pattern for errands is 200-2,000 NCr + relationship, but a favour is a favour first.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Nothing right now, thank you. If I need a hand, you'll be the first to know.

debt.unlock: Semantic flag owes_player or player_owes set

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Money between us? Say it plainly — the ledger keeps the record, not either of us.

choices.text: You owe me — let's settle it.
I owe you — let's settle it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I owe you an apology.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll see you around.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take care. The district's smaller than it looks.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Don't be a stranger — come by any time.

construction_worker.speaker: construction_worker
construction_worker.text: Physical site work, staged builds — that's the job. You learn to read a site the way others read a book.

construction_worker.speaker: construction_worker
construction_worker.text: The yard at the industry edge is where the day starts. Tools, plans, and a foreman who notices everything.

civil_engineer.speaker: civil_engineer
civil_engineer.text: Take a job, draw the plan, estimate the materials, supervise the build, get paid. That's the loop — simple to say, hard to do well.

civil_engineer.speaker: civil_engineer
civil_engineer.text: The site office at the industry edge is my second home. Every build starts as lines on paper.

doctor.speaker: doctor
doctor.text: Clinic shifts in the Civic Quarter. People come in worried and leave lighter — that's the whole job, really.

doctor.speaker: doctor
doctor.text: Diagnosis is mostly listening. The patient usually tells you what's wrong, if you let them finish.

teacher.speaker: teacher
teacher.text: School days run on bells and the children's questions. They keep you honest — they notice everything.

teacher.speaker: teacher
teacher.text: Teaching is half subject, half patience. The certificate gets you in the door; the children decide if you stay.

police_officer.speaker: police_officer
police_officer.text: Patrols through the Civic Quarter and the market hours. Most days it's quiet — quiet is good.

police_officer.speaker: police_officer
police_officer.text: The station's in the Civic Quarter. We keep the peace; the district does the rest.

taxi_driver.speaker: taxi_driver
taxi_driver.text: Fares across all the zones, from the depot at the industry edge. Every passenger is a small story.

taxi_driver.speaker: taxi_driver
taxi_driver.text: A rented CNG today, my own car tomorrow — that's the plan. The road teaches you the city.

chef.speaker: chef
chef.text: Kitchen shifts at the restaurant in Boro Bazar. A good menu is half the business — the other half is showing up.

chef.speaker: chef
chef.text: The market run comes first: fresh ingredients, and a cook who knows the stallholders by name.

software_developer.speaker: software_developer
software_developer.text: Office block in Uptown Heights — deadlines, code, and the occasional remote day. The work follows me home sometimes.

software_developer.speaker: software_developer
software_developer.text: Programming is just breaking a big problem into small ones until none of them scare you anymore.

shop_owner.speaker: shop_owner
shop_owner.text: My shop unit in Boro Bazar — buy stock wholesale, set the price, watch the day. Some months are kind, some aren't.

shop_owner.speaker: shop_owner
shop_owner.text: A tea stall taught me the trade. Small capital, a tenancy, and regulars who remember you.

business_owner.speaker: business_owner
business_owner.text: A company office in Uptown, premises across the zones. The business grows or it doesn't — there's no standing still.

business_owner.speaker: business_owner
business_owner.text: Hiring well is the whole job. A good employee is worth more than a good month.

pilot.speaker: pilot
pilot.text: The regional airport is my workplace — no airport in District 1, so I commute out. The sky's the office; the district is home.

pilot.speaker: pilot
pilot.text: Flying is mostly navigation and patience. The licence took years; the view is worth it.

d1_market.speaker: npc
d1_market.text: Boro Bazar on a busy day — you can hear the whole district in one street.

d1_market.speaker: npc
d1_market.text: Six tea stalls and a market hall. If it's sold anywhere in Rupsha, it's sold here.

d1_oldtown.speaker: npc
d1_oldtown.text: The lanes here are older than the rest of the district put together.

d1_oldtown.speaker: npc
d1_oldtown.text: Repair workshops and walk-up housing — the oldest part of the district, and it shows in the best way.

d1_riverfront.speaker: npc
d1_riverfront.text: The river does something to the air here. Even on a bad day, the promenade helps.

d1_riverfront.speaker: npc
d1_riverfront.text: Watch the sunset from the promenade — the ghat steps, the launches, the whole city slowing down.

d1_midtown.speaker: npc
d1_midtown.text: Six storeys of neighbours. You learn everyone's footsteps in a building like this.

d1_midtown.speaker: npc
d1_midtown.text: Midtown is where the district lives — flats, families, and the starter building.

d1_civic.speaker: npc
d1_civic.text: School, clinic, bank, police station — everything official, all in one quarter.

d1_civic.speaker: npc
d1_civic.text: The Civic Quarter runs on paperwork and patience, in that order.

d1_education.speaker: npc
d1_education.text: College Para — students, bookshops, hostels. The whole quarter runs on exams and the food row.

d1_education.speaker: npc
d1_education.text: The library reading room is the quietest place in the district. Students guard that silence like treasure.

d1_industry.speaker: npc
d1_industry.text: Factories, the depot, the yard. The district's work happens here before the shops open.

d1_industry.speaker: npc
d1_industry.text: Three small factories and a construction yard — noisy, honest work.

d1_park.speaker: npc
d1_park.text: The pond, the walking loop, the benches. Best seat in the district, and it's free.

d1_park.speaker: npc
d1_park.text: Central Park in the morning — walkers, food carts, and the city waking up slowly.

d1_transport.speaker: npc
d1_transport.text: Bus terminal, railway station, rickshaw stands. Everyone leaves from here eventually.

d1_transport.speaker: npc
d1_transport.text: Station Quarter — if you're going anywhere, you start here.

d1_uptown.speaker: npc
d1_uptown.text: Uptown Heights — the office block, the premium shops, and the rooftop restaurant above it all.

d1_uptown.speaker: npc
d1_uptown.text: The high end of the district. Even the air feels more expensive up here.
